next_question: Can a stochastic positive control SPA — where action genuinely changes P(next_state | state) (e.g., 50% deterministic + 50% uniform over CANDIDATES) — validate KSG CMI and likelihood-ratio estimators by achieving positive_control_k3 >= 0.5 bits while preserving |shuffled-action null_mean| < 0.1 bits at N=5000, thereby closing the C3 test-design gap that blocked the frozen verdict?
why_next: The frozen verdict is FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING because no estimator passes both C1 and C3. However, the critical advance is that KSG CMI (|null|=0.0155) and likelihood-ratio (|null|=0.0045) achieve null centering for the first time, breaking the 0.41-bit plug-in PMI floor. The C3 failure is a test-design limitation: the 8-state deterministic SPA produces I(Y;A|Z)=0 by construction for CMI estimators. A stochastic positive control where P(Y|Z,A) != P(Y|Z) is needed to validate KSG/LR sensitivity. If sensitivity is validated, proceed to beyond-Markov K3-K2 testing. If not, the Physics lane must pivot to fundamentally different detection paradigms or production Web data.

established: KSG CMI (sklearn mutual_info_classif k=5) achieves |shuffled-action null_mean|=0.0155 bits on 12-state hash-routed SPA at N=5000 — first estimator to center null near zero. Likelihood-ratio achieves |null|=0.0045 bits. Both <0.1 threshold. Null bias is specific to stratum-partitioned plug-in PMI with Laplace smoothing, not intrinsic to all estimation frameworks. KSG and LR bypass stratum partitioning entirely. (EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440 audit.json claim_ceiling, report.md section 3)

KSG CMI null centering comes at cost of sensitivity: positive_control_k3=0.018 bits (100x below theoretical ~2 bits for deterministic SPA). Null_std 0.000206 (35x smaller than PMI). Estimator near-zero for all inputs. (EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440 result.json:screening.B-KSG-CMI; audit.json V3-ksg_insensitivity_tradeoff)

Likelihood-ratio collapses history: K2=K3=0.104 forced equal, K3-K2=0.0. LR tests action-dependence within each state, ignoring history length. (EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440 result.json:screening.B-LIKELIHOOD-RATIO.k2_value==k3_value; audit.json V4)

Bayesian Dirichlet-Multinomial model comparison is inappropriate for CMI estimation: |null_mean|=213.7 bits (log BF scale), incomparable to bit-scale CMI. (EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440 result.json:screening.B-BAYESIAN-MODEL; audit.json V5)

Parent plug-in PMI estimators replicate exactly: weighted null_mean=0.407 (parent 0.407), K2=0.933, K3=1.221. Stratum bias decomposition identical: +0.736 at 5-9, +0.562 at 10-19, +0.369 at 20-49. (EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440 result.json; audit.json recomputed_parent_replication)

SPA design validated: 48/48 (state,action) pairs with 4 distinct candidates. 0% design-level determinism. C6 and C7 pass. (EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440 result.json:controls.C6-DESIGN-DETERMINISM, C7-SIZE-BUCKETS)

C3 positive control threshold (1.0 bit) is inappropriate for CMI estimators. KSG 0.018, LR 0.241 both significant (p=0.000999) but below bit threshold. A stochastic SPA positive control is needed. (EXP-PHYSICS-35476270440 audit.json V2, controls.C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL)

do_not_assume: C-WEB-DYNAMICS is globally false. All evidence is synthetic in-memory SPA simulation. The frozen FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING reflects test-design limitation, not scientific falsification.
The null bias of ~0.41 bits is evidence against beyond-Markov signal. The bias prevents interpretation but does not falsify underlying dynamics.
KSG CMI sensitivity failure (0.018 bits) on the deterministic SPA means KSG cannot detect action-conditioned dynamics on any SPA. The deterministic SPA is a degenerate test case for CMI.

The frozen FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict closes the orthogonal-estimator pathway. It closes only the current test-design iteration; KSG/LR null centering is a genuine advance that requires a stochastic positive control to complete validation.
Likelihood-ratio test is invalid because K2=K3. The test is valid for action-dependence detection but cannot address conditional-on-history questions (H2) due to history collapse.
Production SPAs generalize from this simulation. The 12-state SPA has 12 states, hash routing, no anti-bot/auth/visual complexity.
This experiment closes the broader C-WEB-DYNAMICS claim. It closes only the current estimator-screening iteration on this specific SPA class.

recommended_action: Design a stochastic positive control SPA where action genuinely changes P(next_state | state) — e.g., 50% deterministic hash routing + 50% uniform random over CANDIDATES, mixed per-transition. This creates I(Y;A|Z) > 0 by construction while preserving the 12-state structure and CANDIDATES framework. Test KSG CMI (k=5, and explore k=3/10) and likelihood-ratio on this stochastic SPA at N=5000 with the same shuffled-action null (N=500, |mean| < 0.1). If KSG achieves both |null| < 0.1 AND positive_control_k3 >= 0.5 bits, proceed to beyond-Markov K3-K2 testing on the 12-state stochastic SPA. If not, the Physics lane must pivot to fundamentally different detection paradigms (entropy rate, channel capacity, causal discovery) or abandon synthetic SPA simulation for production Web data.
